log.msg: Server/health-supervisor.mjs now watches health.mjs itself and cycles its child when the file changes, mirroring server.js's own Server/ watch: an MtimeFilter (so a plain read never looks like an edit), a 500ms debounce (server.js's own number, so several quick saves cycle the child once), and `node --check` before ever touching the live child -- a file that does not even parse leaves the old, working child running untouched. No boot-test dance beyond that, on purpose: health.mjs opens no port, so there is nothing to boot-test against (the file's own prior reasoning, unchanged). A deliberate cycle rides the existing crash-handling exit path (same respawn code, backoff reset to the start value, a distinct log line so it reads as 'cycled' not 'crashed').

Proved the new watch+debounce+check logic in isolation, NOT against the live supervisor or its real heartbeat.json (touching those was the exact thing I was told not to do). Built a byte-for-byte copy of the real, current Server/health-supervisor.mjs with only its two path constants and its MtimeFilter import redirected to a scratch dir (everything else -- the watch/debounce/check/cycle code under test -- untouched), forked a private throwaway process against a dummy child script (not the real health.mjs), and drove it through three cases: (1) one valid edit -> exactly one clean cycle, old pid replaced by a new one, logged as 'cycled' with no crash/backoff framing; (2) five rapid edits within 250ms -> exactly ONE cycle, not five -- the debounce collapsing them; (3) a syntax-broken save -> zero cycles, the old child kept running, logged as 'syntax error, NOT cycling'. All three passed. Killed only my own private test supervisor/child afterward (a different pid than the live ones); confirmed the real supervisor (34636) and child (34924) were never touched, heartbeat still fresh, restarts still 0.

HONEST BOOTSTRAP NOTE, and I did not act on it myself: this new watch code cannot take effect until the LIVE health-supervisor.mjs process (pid 34636, started before this code existed) is restarted once by hand -- same as server.js's own documented 'saving server.js does not upgrade a supervisor already running.' Per the coordinator's direct instruction, I did not attempt this restart and am not asking anyone to run it for me here -- it is being placed on the owner's own board with the exact command.
